title: Web UI
covers: Websites, landing pages, web apps, dashboards, extension popups and app screens: anything a person sees and clicks.

stakeholders.who: First-time visitor on a phone or a laptop (the client's own customer)
cares_about: understanding what this is and what to do next
a page that works and does not jump while loading
would_notice: text clipped or a sideways scroll at phone width
placeholder words, a default tab title or favicon
a button or link that does nothing
a blank area or an endless spinner instead of a message
light grey text that is hard to read

stakeholders.who: Keyboard or screen-reader user, or someone with low vision
cares_about: reaching every control without a mouse
controls whose label says what they do
would_notice: no visible focus ring when pressing Tab
form errors shown only in red

stakeholders.who: The business owner who commissioned the site
cares_about: their facts, brand and voice shown correctly
a site that looks made for them, not a template
would_notice: a wrong phone number, address, price or opening hours
colours or a logo that do not match the brand
one page that looks like a different site
a template look they have seen elsewhere

stakeholders.who: A professional front-end reviewer who opens DevTools
cares_about: a clean console and network tab
layout built on one spacing and type scale

first_ten_seconds: Open the page cold at phone width: can you say what it is, who it is for and what to do next?
Is the main action visible without scrolling, at phone and at desktop width?
Does anything look unfinished: overflowing text, a missing image, placeholder words, a default tab title or favicon?
Does it look made for this business, or like a template you have seen before?

checks.claim: Every changed page was screenshotted at phone, tablet and desktop width, and each image was actually read, not just captured.
checks.how_to_inspect: Serve on localhost (never file://); screenshot at about 360-375, 768 and 1280-1440 px (a native app: a small and a large phone); open each image and write one line on what you checked at that width.
checks.evidence_required: The evidence record craft-evidence-web-ui.json in the run folder (one screenshot per viewport per page, each with a line on what was looked at), and the exit 0 of forge-craft-evidence.cjs check --run <id> --type web-ui.

source.quote: must show real responsive screenshot evidence (mobile + tablet + desktop)

checks.claim: No sideways scroll, clipped or overlapping text, or broken layout at any of those widths.
checks.how_to_inspect: At 360 px compare document.documentElement.scrollWidth with the viewport width; scan each screenshot for text running past its box, overlapping elements and single orphaned words in headings.
checks.evidence_required: The scrollWidth reading at 360 px and the screenshot paths with any overflow named.

source.quote: No horizontal overflow, clipped text, or broken layout at any tested breakpoint.

checks.claim: Every visible word, image and number is real content for this client: no lorem ipsum, 'your headline here', TODO, example.com, grey placeholder images or test data.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the built output for lorem, placeholder, todo, example.com, test and 555-; look at every image in the screenshots.
checks.evidence_required: The search command with zero hits, or the hits and how each was fixed.

source.quote: No placeholder/Lorem/test/mock content in anything headed for prod.

checks.claim: Business facts (name, phone, e-mail, address, prices, opening hours, team names) match the client's own source exactly.
checks.how_to_inspect: List every business fact on the pages and compare each with the brief or the client's material; any fact without a source is removed or sent to the owner as a question.
checks.evidence_required: A fact list with the source of each fact.

checks.claim: On the first screen, at phone and at desktop width, a visitor can tell what this is, who it is for and what to do next.
checks.how_to_inspect: Look only at the top of the 360 px and 1280 px screenshots and write the three answers; a missing answer is a defect.
checks.evidence_required: The three answers and the two screenshot paths.

source.quote: Mobile and desktop layout intact; primary CTA clear.

checks.claim: Every data view, search and form has a designed loading, empty and error state whose words say what happened and what to do.
checks.how_to_inspect: Force each state (loading, empty, error, partial, success, no permission) with no data, DevTools network throttling, a failing request, offline mode or a signed-out user, and screenshot it.
checks.evidence_required: In the evidence record: one screenshot per state per view, or n/a with the reason (for example: the page shows no data, or there is no sign-in).

source.quote: working nav/forms/search with loading + empty + error states

checks.claim: Every link and button does something real: no href="#", no dead navigation item, no 404 from an internal link.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run a link checker on the served site and click the main navigation and every call to action once.
checks.evidence_required: The link-check output with zero broken links and a note of the clicks made.

checks.claim: Forms say what is wrong next to the field, in words, and the success state tells the visitor what happens next.
checks.how_to_inspect: Submit each form empty, with one wrong value and with valid data; screenshot all three results.
checks.evidence_required: Three screenshots per form and the endpoint that received the valid submit.

source.quote: Forms validate input and hit a real endpoint; clear error + success states.

checks.claim: Body text, small text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and control edges), including text placed on images.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run axe or Lighthouse accessibility, then measure text on images and hover states by hand with a contrast checker.
checks.evidence_required: The checker output and the hand-measured ratios.

source.quote: Color contrast meets a defensible accessibility bar for body text and interactive elements.

checks.claim: Every interactive element is reachable with Tab in a sensible order, shows a visible focus ring, and works with Enter or Space.
checks.how_to_inspect: Tab through each changed page from the address bar to the footer without the mouse and note anything skipped, trapped or invisible.
checks.evidence_required: A short tab-order note per page, or a recording.

checks.claim: Meaningful images have alt text, decorative images have empty alt, and icon-only buttons and form fields have an accessible name.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run axe, then read the accessibility tree in DevTools for every icon button and input.
checks.evidence_required: The axe result with zero name or alt violations, or the fixes made.

source.quote: keyboard navigation, alt text, ARIA where needed

checks.claim: The console shows zero errors and the network tab no failed requests on every changed page, including its empty and error states.
checks.how_to_inspect: Load each page with DevTools open on the console and network tabs, then trigger the empty and error states.
checks.evidence_required: The console capture per page.

checks.claim: No localhost URLs, debug banners, test buttons, console.log noise, or framework default page titles and favicons.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the build for localhost, 127.0.0.1, console.log and debugger; read document.title and the favicon link of every page.
checks.evidence_required: The search output and the title and favicon of each page.

source.quote: No localhost URLs, debug/test banners, or debug-only UI.

checks.claim: Spacing follows one scale and edges line up: the same gap for the same relationship, headings and text on the same column, icons centred with their labels.
checks.how_to_inspect: Zoom the 1280 px screenshot to 200 percent (or overlay a grid) and compare left edges, card heights and the gaps between sections.
checks.evidence_required: The zoomed screenshot with each misalignment named (element and pixel offset).

source.quote: spacing, alignment, contrast, copy, empty and error states, naming, units, the first ten seconds

checks.claim: Body text is at least 16 px on phones, lines hold about 45 to 80 characters, and line height is about 1.5 or more.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read the computed font size and line height of body text in DevTools at 360 and 1280 px and count the characters of a typical line.
checks.evidence_required: The measured values per width.

source.rationale: Small, long or cramped lines are what a reader feels as 'hard to read' before they can say why.

checks.claim: The design is specific to this client (their colours, type pairing, imagery and tone), not a generic template look.
checks.how_to_inspect: Compare the first screen with the brand assets and ask whether this hero could belong to any other business; walk the guidance tells list (lens --type web-ui) and name each tell you find; name what makes it theirs.
checks.evidence_required: One sentence naming the brand-specific choices, the tells found (or none), with the screenshot path.

source.quote: uniform card grids, centered-hero-plus-gradient-blob, safe gray-on-white with one accent color

checks.claim: Before any markup a token plan was written and held against the brief: 4 to 6 named hex colours with a job each, the type roles, one spacing scale and a layout sketch per page; the build uses only those tokens.
checks.how_to_inspect: Open the plan (guidance before_build), trace every colour, face and section to the brief or the brand assets, then search the built CSS for colours and spacing values outside the plan.
checks.evidence_required: The plan's path, the brief lines it was checked against, and the off-plan values found (or none); n/a only for a change that adds no new visual design.

source.rationale: A design chosen before building, from the brief, is what stops the framework defaults and the generated look from filling the gaps.

checks.claim: All pages and states share one type scale, colour set, button style and spacing; no page looks like a different site.
checks.how_to_inspect: Put the screenshots of every page side by side and compare headings, buttons and section spacing.
checks.evidence_required: The side-by-side screenshot paths and any page that deviates.

source.section: 2. Sloppy / quality complaints, by deliverable type
source.quote: Visual coherence across all views, not a few pages.

checks.claim: On a phone every control is big enough to tap (about 44 by 44 px) and nothing needs hover to work.
checks.how_to_inspect: Measure the smallest links and icon buttons in DevTools at 360 px; check that menus and tooltips open with a tap.
checks.evidence_required: The smallest target size found, and its fix when under about 44 px.

source.quote: Touch targets are usable on mobile

checks.claim: Animation explains a change instead of decorating, respects prefers-reduced-motion, and both light and dark theme are checked when the project has both.
checks.how_to_inspect: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion and the colour scheme in DevTools rendering settings and screenshot the main page again.
checks.evidence_required: The reduced-motion and theme screenshots, or N/A with the reason.

guidance.precedence: The brief's explicit visual direction (named colours, fonts, a reference image, a brand guide, a style the owner asked for) always wins over this lens: follow the brief, and use the lens only where the brief is silent.
before_build: Colours: 4 to 6 named tokens with a hex value and one job each (for example text, background, surface, main action, accent, warning), taken from the brand assets when they exist.
Type roles: one face for headings and one for body text (two families at most), with a size scale of about 5 to 7 steps and the line height for each role.
Spacing: one scale (for example 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 px) and nothing outside it; radius and shadow as two or three named steps as well.
Layout sketch per page: the sections in order, what sits on the first screen at phone and at desktop width, and the one memorable element.
Hold the plan against the brief before building: every token and section traces to the brief or the brand assets; write down each choice you made yourself and why.

tells.tell: Framework default colours: the stock blue or indigo button, grey text on white everywhere, one lonely accent.
tells.instead: The named colours from the token plan, derived from the brand.

tells.tell: A centred headline with a sub line and two buttons, followed by three identical cards with an icon on top.
tells.instead: A first screen built around this client's own offer, photo, number or proof.

tells.tell: Every section is the same grid of equal cards, so the page has no rhythm.
tells.instead: Let the content choose the form: a list, a quote, a full-width image, a table, a timeline.

tells.tell: Blurred gradient blobs or glowing orbs behind the hero that have nothing to do with the business.
tells.instead: Imagery or texture that belongs to this business, or calm space.

tells.tell: Paddings and gaps that follow no scale: 13 px here, 22 px there, each section different.
tells.instead: Only the spacing steps from the token plan, the same gap for the same relationship.

tells.tell: Lorem ipsum or empty phrases such as 'Unlock your potential', 'Seamless solutions' or 'Welcome to our website'.
tells.instead: Specific words: what it is, for whom, the price or the next step.

tells.tell: Buttons and links that change on hover but show nothing on keyboard focus or when pressed.
tells.instead: A hover, focus-visible and active state on every clickable element.

tells.tell: One family at one weight for headings and body, so nothing leads the eye.
tells.instead: The two type roles from the plan, with a clear size step between them.

tells.tell: The same soft grey drop shadow on every surface.
tells.instead: A small depth system: base, raised and floating, tinted towards the palette.

tells.tell: Emoji or icons from several sets used as feature icons.
tells.instead: One icon family at one stroke weight, or no icons at all.

copy_rules: Body text lines hold about 45 to 80 characters (aim near 65): give text columns a maximum width instead of letting lines run across a wide screen.
One memorable element per page: a striking photo, a bold number, a quote or a signature illustration. One, not five that compete.
A heading says something only this client can say; a heading that could sit on any other site is rewritten.
Button labels name the action and its result ('Book a table', 'Get the price list'), never 'Click here' or 'Submit'.
An empty state says what is missing, why, and the one next step (with a button when there is one); never a blank area or a bare 'No data'.
An error message says in plain words what went wrong and how to fix it, keeps what the user typed, and never shows only a code or blames the user.

rule_lines.rule: Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 against its background; at least 3:1 for large text (about 24 px, or 19 px bold) and for control borders and focus rings. Measure text on images too.
Every focusable element shows a clear indicator on keyboard focus (:focus-visible); an outline is never removed without a visible replacement.
Tap targets are about 44 by 44 CSS px, never under 24 px without space around them; links inside running text are the only exception.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, movement and parallax stop or become a simple fade; nothing flashes more than three times a second.
Every input has a visible label tied to it; placeholder text is never the only label, and colour is never the only signal of an error.
Every img and video carries width and height (or sits in an aspect-ratio box), is served near its display size in a modern format, and loads lazily below the first screen.
Nothing moves after the first paint: space is reserved for fonts, images, banners and late content; aim for a layout shift (CLS) under 0.1.
The largest first-screen element shows fast (LCP under about 2.5 s, INP under about 200 ms on a mid-range phone); numbers measured on localhost are labelled local and indicative.
At most two font families and a few weights; fonts use font-display swap or optional, and the first-screen face is preloaded.
Each screen has one primary action that clearly leads; secondary actions look secondary.
Every action answers within about a second (a pressed state, a skeleton or progress), and a longer wait says what is happening.
Form errors appear next to the field in words, and focus moves to the first field that needs fixing.

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: the page wiggles left and right at 360 px because one element is wider than the screen
the browser tab says 'Vite + React' or 'React App' next to the framework favicon
lorem ipsum, 'Your headline here', example.com, 555 phone numbers, grey stock boxes
a navigation item or button that points to # or does nothing when clicked
a heading a few pixels off the text column, cards of uneven height, icons sitting above their labels
each section has a different padding and the gaps follow no scale
a white gap or an endless spinner when there is no data or the request fails
light grey body text on white that cannot be read in daylight
pressing Tab moves somewhere, but nothing on screen shows where
a centred hero with a gradient blob and three identical cards, as on many generated sites
